We have a tool get_protein_sequence that can retrieve the protein sequence encoded by a human gene. It says species optional default "Homo sapiens". So we can call get_protein_sequence for gene "BRCA1" and "BRCA2" for species "Homo sapiens" and "Pan troglodytes". The function returns any. We need to call it twice for each species? Actually we need to retrieve the protein sequences for both genes in both species. So four calls: get_protein_sequence(gene="BRCA1", species="Homo sapiens"), get_protein_sequence(gene="BRCA2", species="Homo sapiens"), get_protein_sequence(gene="BRCA1", species="Pan troglodytes"), get_protein_sequence(gene="BRCA2", species="Pan troglodytes").

We need to use the function calls. The function signature: get_protein_sequence takes an object with gene: string, species?: string. So we need to call it with JSON arguments. We'll do separate calls. Then we need to output the sequences. The function returns any; presumably a string or maybe a dict with sequence. We'll just output the returned value. We'll need to handle the function calls. We'll do them sequentially.
